admission.justification: The runtime-scoped shared store and fresh per-operation discovery prevent one runtime or old in-process answer deciding another start; pre-creation validation uses only parts for which current or saved offers are actually known.

applicability: Every consumer of the configured Paseo catalog when it needs current launch-choice or provider-capability information: launcher views and rechecks, new role starts and their preparation, tool-server acceptance/status checks, caller-harness/native-tool checks, settings initialization that needs offered harnesses, and settings-driven explainer starts.
conditions: The shared stored answer is scoped by install prefix, home, listen address and runtime version.
Each top-level operation requests fresh host data; nested work in the same operation may share its answer.
Unavailable parts use only their corresponding successful saved part; unknown parts are not represented as empty offered sets.
Explicitly unoffered choices in a known answer are refused before durable preparation.
Every catalog consumer uses the same configured-host resolver and saved-part policy.
exclusions: A saved-only display is not authority to start without the fresh request finishing.
Unavailable metadata does not prove a configured value unsupported.
No promise of successful host creation follows from unchecked choices.
Service-tier capability behavior retains its separate owner; freshness does not authorize permission-bearing start arguments.
A repeated receipt-bound request retains the recorded call and choices; do not turn catalog freshness into reselecting an already recorded launch.
Permission-mode defaults are explicitly excluded from R214 name-map removal, and unknown offerings do not grant permission authority.
statement: Every launcher view and role start asks the configured Paseo runtime for current choices. A view reads full offers; a start reads provider/model metadata and then only the selected model's features. Within one operation the answer may be shared, but no process-lifetime cache controls later views or starts. Unavailable parts use the shared last successful answer with its timestamp; a part with no current or saved answer leaves configured values unchecked. Known agent/model/effort choices are validated before workspace or enclosure creation. Launcher rechecks, role-start preparation, tool-server checks, caller-harness checks, settings initialization and settings-driven explainer starts use this same resolver and saved-part policy.
